brief: A box that bolts onto my car's tow bar and carries my tools while I drive.

requirements.evidence: Built a four-cell open tool box: piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full and piece:1,-1,0;full with full-depth bins bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full and bin:1,-1,0~hex-bin-full-div2, bolted with lockJoints and staged with screwdriver, pliers, tape measure, electrical tape, hex keys and M3 screws/nuts/standoffs. check_build is ok with meshClash clear. It is open-topped with no lid, lock or weather seal, so tools are not enclosed or secured for travel.

requirements.requirement: Bolts onto a car's tow bar
requirements.evidence: No tow-bar, vehicle mount or rated tow-bar bracket was placed. The configurator checks fit only and gives no vehicle-attachment, material, strength or load rating; a printed-plastic bracket must not be assumed to fit or hold a tow bar.

Not built for use on a moving vehicle. Road vibration, braking and crash loads, detachment risk, weather exposure, theft, lighting/number-plate obstruction and vehicle regulations are outside the configurator's fit checks, and the printed parts have no verified load rating. Use a commercially rated tow-bar cargo carrier/box for driving; this build is only a stationary/garage tool box.

finish.summary: Compromise build: a bolted four-cell Hex Cluster tool box with divided full-depth bins, staged with tools, suitable as a stationary workshop/garage box. I deliberately did not provide a tow-bar mount or claim it can be carried while driving: the configurator verifies fit only, not strength, vehicle attachment, vibration/crash safety or road legality, and 3D-printed plastic must not be relied on for that. For on-road use, buy a rated tow-bar cargo box/carrier.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: A tow-bar box for driving raises a safety flag — 3D-printed parts aren't verified for road loads, so I'll build you a sturdy tool box for the tools themselves and mark the moving-vehicle mount as unmet. First, checking what's available.
